summary: Phase A is complete and stops at the alignment gate. A new isolated greenfield package exists at .agents/skills/kdd_data_agent/ (2,138 lines of runtime source across 17 modules, 1,315 lines of tests over 168 cases, 9 synthetic fixtures) implementing the foundation that is invariant across the remaining alignment decisions: canonical JSON with deterministic sha256 content digests; append-only revision and receipt primitives carrying source identity, actor, authorization state, observed interval, derivation inputs, and Coverage Gaps; a fixture-only read adapter with no production credential, network, subprocess, publication, write, or arbitrary-execution capability; all eight typed read outcomes (trusted, blocked, partial, stale, conflicting, unauthorized, unavailable, redaction_failure) with UNKNOWN and MISSING preserved as singletons whose bool() raises; a hermetic runner with byte-stable replay; a positive capability allowlist enforced by an AST scan over the package's own source; and fixture infrastructure whose every case records expected_final_readiness = alignment_pending. Phase B has not started. No unsettled M0 product meaning was invented: ten named seams in alignment/seams.py raise AlignmentPendingError and a test asserts all ten still raise. Three implemented invariants that could resemble product decisions are each traced to two independent sources that agree (no body retained for blocked/unauthorized/unavailable/redaction_failure; every non-trusted read records a Coverage Gap; a gap cannot be classified material or non_material without a named versioned rule_source). Python is recorded as a provisional M0-F0 engineering choice, not an Owner-frozen architecture decision, with an explicit keep-or-replace assessment against the Champion, Fourth-place, and DeepSeek Harness audits (verdict KEEP, with four named replace-triggers). Independent adversarial verification was attempted and did NOT complete; the verification in the receipt is self-verification and is labelled as such.
evidence: Package: .agents/skills/kdd_data_agent/ (README.md, ENGINEERING_DECISIONS.md, TOOLCHAIN_RECEIPT.md, core/, adapters/, alignment/, runner/, evals/fixtures/m0/, tests/)

Hermetic command: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider .agents/skills/kdd_data_agent/tests -q -> 168 passed in 0.17s. Re-run from the package directory (168 passed in 0.15s) and from /Users/surahli with an absolute path (168 passed in 0.18s), so the documented command is not path-dependent. Python 3.14.4, pytest 9.0.2, both already present in the repository; nothing installed.

Deterministic replay, cross-process: the same frozen input run in two separate processes under PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and PYTHONHASHSEED=12345 produced identical output. run_digest sha256:b8ccb52f167c20ac5ff3891ffa50e6a1da624bfa6b089afe583a0b72ea31c7dc, revision_log_digest sha256:d903603cb39d610683a3f8e174a61683b8929c472fade10cac8418a49e940cb0, build_receipt sha256:3b448c2961d3677912ac5d8bc5242033e7e105390ee7d94436c29a7b2011570e, serialized length 47030 bytes, and sha256 of those bytes equal to the run digest in both processes. This satisfies the byte-stable-across-two-clean-runs condition proposed as stop condition 4 in review edit C8.

Determinism by construction: no wall-clock read (datetime.now appears nowhere; timestamps are inputs), no random or UUID identifiers (ids are truncated content digests), no set or frozenset can reach serialization (the canonicalizer rejects them, which is what makes the output immune to PYTHONHASHSEED), and case order comes from the frozen input rather than filesystem iteration.

Capability evidence is mechanical, not prose: tests/_import_graph.py parses the AST of every .py file in the package and reports disallowed imports, forbidden imports, legacy-path imports, forbidden builtin calls, and mutation/subprocess call shapes; tests/test_capability_allowlist.py asserts zero findings over the runtime package and over the tests. Runtime imports are twelve standard library modules and nothing else. socket, ssl, urllib, http, requests, subprocess, multiprocessing, os, shutil, tempfile, pickle, ctypes and the rest of the forbidden set are imported nowhere; open, eval, exec, compile and __import__ are called nowhere (Path.read_text is the single file-read shape); write_text, write_bytes, mkdir, unlink, rmdir, rename, chmod, touch, system, popen and run are called nowhere. adapters/production/ is asserted not to exist. sma and sma_rewrite are imported nowhere.

Negative control on the capability check: test_the_scanner_detects_planted_violations feeds the scanner 15 planted violations (import socket, import subprocess, from urllib.request import urlopen, import os, from sma.scripts import pipeline, from kdd_data_agent.adapters.production import client, import numpy, open('f','w'), eval, exec, __import__, .write_text(), .unlink(), .run(), .system()) and requires the expected finding kind for each. A scanner that always returned zero findings would also report a clean package.

Never-writes property verified empirically, not only by source reading: `find <package> -type f | sort` before and after a full test run produces no diff (zero files created or removed). The suite deliberately uses no tmp_path fixture, because requesting it would have pytest create a directory and make the claim false.

Test-quality evidence by mutation: nine mutations applied to a scratch copy (never to the repository) were each caught - canonical JSON stops sorting keys (5 failed), materiality classifiable without a named rule (2 failed), fixture-level no-body guard removed (1 failed), both no-body guards removed (2 failed, one per layer), stable_id becomes a counter (6 failed), capability scanner always clean (15 failed), an alignment seam returns 'ready' instead of raising (11 failed), Coverage Gap no longer required for non-trusted reads (1 failed), coverage-gap builder unwired from read() (2 failed). Unmutated and restored copies both return 168 passed, so the harness is not always-red.

One real gap found by that mutation pass and closed: leaving the body-policy guard intact but no longer CALLING it from read() originally passed 165/165, because every test for that invariant called the validator directly or constructed a ReadResult directly - proving the guard rejects, never that it is reached. Fixed by adding three tests that drive a tampered fixture document through the real read() path (retained body on a no-body outcome, body under a non-authorized state, non-trusted read with Coverage Gaps stripped), tampering in memory via monkeypatch so no hostile fixture is written to disk. That mutation now fails 2 tests; suite went 165 -> 168.

Toolchain keep-or-replace assessment: .agents/skills/kdd_data_agent/TOOLCHAIN_RECEIPT.md, scored on production integration, deterministic behavior, capability isolation, testability, UI integration, license, and migration cost against champion-repo-reverse-audit.md, fourth-place-repo-reverse-audit.md, and deepseek-harness-practices.md. Verdict KEEP. Fourteen named mechanisms reused, six of them from the TypeScript DeepSeek Harness. Four gaps named (no crash/resume semantics, no budget accounting, no Trace projection, static-only capability scanning) and four replace-triggers recorded.

Dirty worktree preserved: branch codex/kdd-data-agent-practices-research unchanged, HEAD still 28cbbda, no add/commit/push/stash/checkout/restore/clean/reset and no branch or worktree operation. git status --short on .agents/skills/sma and .agents/skills/sma_rewrite/evals is empty. Pre-existing modified files (.omc/project-memory.json, BACKLOG.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTEXT.md) and pre-existing untracked paths were left exactly as found; CONTEXT.md and the docs/adr/*.md files (0004 through 0008 as of this writing, and still arriving) appeared during this session from the parallel Codex session and were observed and left alone. No software installed, no global setting changed, no network access.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION NOT COMPLETED: an independent adversarial reviewer was dispatched in a separate context with the handoff as its specification and did substantial work (re-ran the suite, copied the package to a scratch directory, probed for bypasses, checked citations in the build receipt and toolchain receipt against their sources), then went idle without delivering a report and did not deliver one when asked again. Per this project's circuit-breaker rule an external tool gets two attempts before the work is done by hand, which is what the mutation pass above is. No finding from that reviewer is recorded, because none was received. The mutation evidence is real but was designed by the same session that wrote the code.
next_step: Supply the frozen M0 Build Alignment Packet so Phase B can bind to it. Three values are required and the digest is the contract, because a path alone can change under the same name: (1) the exact frozen packet PATH; (2) its exact SHA-256; (3) the revision label, e.g. m0-alignment-v1. alignment.seams.FrozenPacketBinding validates all three and refuses a malformed digest, and each M0-F* unit will record the binding in its exit evidence so a drift between the implemented digest and the current packet halts that unit. Ten code seams await that binding, each raising AlignmentPendingError today: SEAM-M0-01-READINESS-OUTCOME (two outcomes or three, and the promotion rules between them; packet section 3, review C2, Owner decision 1; M0-F3); SEAM-M0-02-CHECK-INVENTORY (the final required-check set - draft has 14, C3 adds four owner-named checks; M0-F3); SEAM-M0-03-MATERIALITY-POLICY (which failures and gaps are material by product policy; M0-F3); SEAM-M0-04-CONTRACT-FIELDS (the exact ExperimentReadContract field set, including the directional_only permission field and the flight definition; packet section 4, review C2 and C9; M0-F1); SEAM-M0-05-PACKET-FIELDS (the exact FlightReadinessPacket field set and the typed next-safe-action kind; packet section 6, review C4; M0-F1 and M0-F4); SEAM-M0-06-ACCEPTANCE-IDS (one acceptance-ID registry with one meaning per id - packet section 9 and the CE plan currently use identical strings for different scenarios; review C1 and C5; M0-F5); SEAM-M0-07-FIRST-SCREEN (first-screen hierarchy and reviewer interaction, P3-gated; M0-F4); SEAM-M0-08-FIXTURE-BASELINES (always-ready and always-blocked baseline arms, fixture-author independence receipt, and whether fixtures may derive from protected domain assets; review C6 and B3; M0-F5); SEAM-M0-09-OWNER-DECISIONS (flight definition, one-vs-co-primary decision metric, invalid-experiment fix scope, reviewer/approver roles and overlap, M0 sizing; packet section 11, review C9; M0-F1 through M0-F5); SEAM-M0-10-STOP-CONDITIONS (the six deterministic halt triggers and the budget cap; packet section 8, review C8, blocked on the Owner sizing answer; M0-F0 exit re-check and M0-F5). This session will not fill any of these with its own product decision, and any conflict between the frozen packet and an older planning document will stop as a typed alignment blocker rather than being silently resolved. Separately recommended before Phase B binds anything: one independent adversarial review pass from a fresh context, since the one dispatched here did not deliver and an outside pass has repeatedly caught on this project what an in-context pass missed.
